VERDICT: BLOCK

## Blocking
- e8680316 (commit subject) — The commit is typed `fix(waves)`, but the change only rewords one doc comment in a `_test.go` file. CONTRIBUTING.md "Commits & releases" says "the type prefix isn't cosmetic", because release-please builds CHANGELOG.md and the version bump from it. `.release-please-config.json` maps `fix` to "Bug Fixes", so the next release notes would list "waves: stop calling headless Session nil" as a user-facing bug fix when no behaviour changed. Repo precedent for this exact kind of edit uses `docs`/`test`: d9662b94 "docs(terminate,waves): retire headless nil claim" and 3265a2a7 "test(outcome): name classifySignalLine in stale test comments". Retype it as `docs(waves): …` or `test(waves): …`.

## Non-blocking
- cmd/launcher/internal/waves/session_test.go:11-13 — The parenthetical "(what headless callers pass)" repeats a list of callers outside this package, and the `Session` type doc at session.go:5-16 already records the same fact. That kind of claim is what went stale and caused this issue. Pointing at the field doc instead (e.g. "see Session.Limiter") would stay accurate longer.
- cmd/launcher/internal/waves/session_test.go:11-13 — The comment now describes the non-nil Session with a nil Limiter path as "the same fallback", but the test only calls `RunContinuous(c, nil, …)`. A reader could assume this test pins the headless path too. The statement is true from continuous.go:197-206, and the issue says a second case is optional, so this is a suggestion only.
- cmd/launcher/internal/waves/continuous.go:203 — "Headless (CONTINUOUS_DISPATCH) and every nil-Session call site" is still accurate, because headless callers reach this branch through a nil Limiter. But it is a third copy of the same caller inventory and can go stale the same way. It is out of scope for this issue, so it's a possible follow-up.
I fixed the blocking review finding: the commit is now typed `test(waves)` instead of `fix(waves)`. Release notes will list it under "Tests" rather than "Bug Fixes", which matches the earlier `test(outcome)` commit for stale test comments. The branch is still one commit (`2170066e`) and was already up to date with `origin/main` (e5fccdca), so the rebase changed nothing.

I also folded two of the reviewer's non-blocking points into the same commit. The comment on `TestRunContinuous_NilSession_FallsBackToFixedLimiter` in `cmd/launcher/internal/waves/session_test.go` now:
- says the test only pins the nil-Session case;
- points at `Session.Limiter` for the nil-Limiter path headless callers take.

I kept the "(what headless callers pass)" wording because the issue's acceptance criteria require it. I dropped the third point, the caller list in the `continuous.go:203` comment. That comment is still accurate and this branch doesn't touch that file.

## Non-blocking
- cmd/launcher/internal/waves/session_test.go:13 — The phrase "(what headless callers pass)" is broader than the path it describes. Two of the three headless call sites (main.go:1712 and selective.go:68) call `waves.Dispatch`, and the Session.Limiter doc (session.go:13-15) says Dispatch never reads that field, so only the headless `RunContinuous` caller (main.go:1927) actually takes this fallback. Writing "headless RunContinuous callers" would be more precise, though the comment sits on a RunContinuous test, so in context it reads correctly.
